Plan: a jurisdiction-agnostic R package for plan-enabled capacity

Source: PLAN.md

Package: plancap (free on CRAN; no R package of that name on GitHub). Status (20 November 2026):

  • Stage 0 done. Gate met: R CMD check green on Windows, macOS and Linux (devel, release, oldrel) at github.com/faceteconomics/plancap. Codecov upload is non-fatal until Codecov is linked (needs CODECOV_TOKEN).
  • Stage 1 built (rulebook). Schema (inst/schema/rulebook.schema.json), R constructors, YAML/JSON/XLSX I/O (all lossless, tested), validation, rule_table(), set_rule()/extend_rulebook()/extends:, metres/feet, restricted formulas. Exampleton rulebook hand-written. Gate: the three capacityengine bundles convert and validate (data-raw/convert_capacityengine.R, reports in data-raw/conversion/): Wellington and Christchurch carry every field; Auckland carries all 217 precincts but 13 fields remain, listed in its report and unmodelled register (see Stage 1 follow-ups below).

Stage 1 follow-ups (for stage 4, engine)

  • Auckland Height Variation Control: class_field, height_conversion_table, passthrough_below/above_m, between_bands (mapped total height to occupiable height) and the overlay sub_areas of the height-sensitive area. Needs an overlay “height conversion” construct; design with the engine.
  • value_from: existing_dwelling_setback_average (SCA front yard set from the neighbours): needs a “measured” value source; v1 net-of-existing work.
  • CfGS-fidelity fields (cfgs_large_site_area_per_dwelling_m2) deliberately not carried.
  • Design additions made in stage 1 that the engine must honour: replaces_setbacks (an override replaces only the named setback kinds), additions, sub-area total_group, plane angle_by_orientation, vertical_above, max_setback_above, conversion min_one_dwelling_floor.
  • The Wellington extract (real example data, Q16) is still to do: needs the capacity-wellington layers cut to ~1,500 parcels with its rulebook. Decisions so far are recorded in section 11.

1. Purpose and scope

An R package that, given parcel boundaries and planning rules, estimates the floorspace and dwellings a plan enables on each site, and then summarises and plots the result. It generalises the method built and tested in capacityengine (Auckland, Christchurch, Wellington) so that any jurisdiction can be modelled by entering its rules, with no package code written.

In scope:

  • A rule model (the “rulebook”) that holds every rule type the capacity project has handled, entered by file, by R functions, or by spreadsheet.
  • Site preparation from any parcel layer: zone splitting, boundary classification, frontage, rear sites, zone adjacency, optional terrain.
  • The 2.5D storey-stack envelope engine and the three yield paths (volumetric, density, hybrid).
  • Summary, comparison and explanation functions.
  • A plotting family with one consistent, publication-quality look.
  • CRAN-standard documentation, tests, and a pkgdown site; public GitHub repo.

Out of scope (stays in capacityengine or the council projects):

  • Data fetching from LINZ, ArcGIS REST, council servers; region tiling and caches; the Shiny explorers; HBA bridges; Auckland-specific scripts.
  • Feasibility, infrastructure, and market take-up. The package estimates plan-enabled capacity only, and says so in every print method.

Carried-over principles (these were each earned the hard way in the project):

  1. Never invent a rule value. Every number in a rulebook carries a source (citation). Missing source is a validation warning, not silent.
  2. Flag, don’t drop. Every input site appears in every output, with flag codes explaining zero or NA results. Totals always reconcile to inputs.
  3. Floor area is the primary output; dwellings are a derived view with the conversion assumptions printed alongside.
  4. Gross, blank-slate capacity by default. Net of existing is an optional hook if the user supplies existing floorspace or dwellings.
  5. Alternative standards are modelled as variants, never merged; the user picks the reporting variant (or “max”, “min”, “all”).
  6. Unmodelled rules are registered with the direction of effect (overstates / understates / either), and reported with the results.

2. Relationship to capacityengine

Recommended (Q2): a clean new package, written fresh against a generalised schema, porting the tested algorithms (not the file layout). capacityengine is left alone; later it can depend on the new package and keep only its NZ data adapters, scenarios and apps. The new package’s test suite inherits the hand-checked cases (e.g. S039789: 24 setbacks exact; the HIRB formula; the reflex-corner wedges; the “touching is not overlapping” adjacency cases).

What is ported, generalised:

capacityengine New package Generalisation
YAML bundle + JSON Schema rulebook S3 object, YAML/JSON/XLSX/R entry NZ terms renamed to neutral ones (see 3.2); NPS zone keys become user zone keys
build_sites, split_sites_by_zone prepare_sites() parcel+title amalgamation becomes an optional group_by
classify_boundaries, frontage, access_legs classify_boundaries() road boundaries from a road layer, OR inferred from gaps / a street centreline layer
apply_zone_adjacency resolve_adjacency() unchanged method (probe far side of midpoint)
build_envelope, apply_caps, enforce_stack_rules build_envelopes() hemisphere-aware orientation rules; units parameter
yield paths estimate_yield() conversion assumptions explicit and required
aggregate_results, diff_scenarios summarise_capacity(), compare_capacity() much richer, see section 6
explorer site_rules_scene() explain_site(), plot_site() static ggplot first, interactive optional

3. The rulebook

3.1 Three ways in, one object

rb <- read_rulebook("exampleton.yaml")          # file (YAML or JSON)
rb <- read_rulebook_xlsx("exampleton.xlsx")     # spreadsheet, for non-R users
rb <- rulebook("Exampleton District Plan", units = "m") |>
  add_zone(zone("MRZ", method = "volumetric",
    height   = height_limit(11, roof_allowance = 1, storeys = 3,
                            source = "MRZ-S1"),
    setbacks = list(setback("road", 1.5, source = "MRZ-S4"),
                    setback(c("side", "rear"), 1, source = "MRZ-S4")),
    planes   = plane(angle = 60, start_height = 4,
                     boundaries = c("side", "rear"), source = "MRZ-S3"),
    coverage = ratio(0.5, source = "MRZ-S5"),
    landscaping = ratio(0.2, source = "MRZ-S6")))
  • rulebook_template("new.xlsx") writes an empty, annotated workbook (one sheet per rule family, a citation column on every sheet, dropdowns for enumerations). rulebook_template("new.yaml") does the same in YAML.
  • validate_rulebook(rb) checks schema (structure), semantics (bands contiguous, variants consistent, every zone referenced by the zone map, every overlay type has its required fields) and lint (missing sources, rules nothing will consume — the riparian lesson).
  • write_rulebook(rb, path) round-trips to YAML/JSON/XLSX losslessly (tested by round-trip property tests).
  • print(rb) / summary(rb) give a readable digest; rule_table(rb) gives a long tidy table of every rule, zone, value and citation (a good appendix table for a report).
  • extend_rulebook(base, changes) = the scenario mechanism (extends: in capacityengine): a plan change or sensitivity expressed as a diff. set_rule(rb, zone = "MRZ", "height", 16) for quick what-ifs.

3.2 Rule catalogue (everything handled in the project)

Neutral names first, with the NZ term in brackets. Every rule accepts source, variant, activity_status and conditions (3.3).

Height and storeys - height_limit(value, occupiable, roof_allowance, storeys) — total vs occupiable height (the HVC lesson: mapped height includes roof form). - Storey heights: default, ground-floor height, per-zone; storey count derived as occupiable / intended storeys, never a flat 3 m. - no_limit_stand_in for zones with no height limit, flagged as upper bound. - Absolute height limits (RL above datum) as well as above-ground.

Setbacks (yards) — by boundary class: road, side, rear, internal, common, coastal, riparian, lakeside, reserve, rail, plus user-defined classes keyed to a layer. Options: above_storey, max_value, value_from = "existing_average" (special character front yard), water yards measured from a water layer.

Planes (recession plane / height in relation to boundary / daylight angle / sky exposure plane): angle, start height, set-in, boundaries, orientation_graded (angle by compass bearing; hemisphere-aware), on_southern_boundary_of_neighbour (generalised to facing), exemptions for the front N m or share of depth, datum (ground / boundary / site mean), vertical_above, step-back above a height.

Upper-level setbacks: extra setback above a storey or height, per class.

Site ratios: building coverage, landscaped area, impervious, paved — each a single value or bands by site area; floor area ratio (FAR) max.

Building form: max floorplate, max tower floorplate / dimension, tower separation, building length, building separation, gaps above a height, minimum floorplate (enforced in the stack), minimum building width, site shape factor (min rectangle).

Density: site area per dwelling, dwellings per hectare, minimum site area, vacant site minimum, max dwellings per site, minor dwellings, max / min dwellings across an area (precinct totals), large-site rules (threshold, infrastructure deduction, alternative density), access-width table (frontage/accessway width → max dwellings), minimum dwelling size.

Use mix: residential enabled, business enabled, residential share of floorspace in mixed zones (with source), max floorspace per site / area.

Methods: volumetric (storey stack), density (rule straight to dwellings), hybrid (both, take the lesser).

Overlays (spatial layers that modify rules), with precedence: height_cap, height_override, height_surface (raster/TIN, e.g. airport surfaces, viewshafts, sunlight admission planes), height_bands (a mapped height converted via a table, the HVC case), exclusion (subtract geometry: hazards, designations, water yards), parameter_override (edit named zone parameters, e.g. special character), flag_only. Each can be default_enabled: false and switched on in a scenario. Partial coverage: a surface caps only the part of a site it covers (engine item 368, done properly from the start).

Areas (precinct / sub-precinct / specific control / overlay zone): overrides, additions, per-zone overrides, sub-areas keyed by a field.

Zone adjacency: rules that switch on the zone across the boundary (business yards and planes), with zone families for set membership.

Conversion: floorspace → dwellings (dwelling size, circulation and efficiency allowances, minimum-one-dwelling floor), shown in every output that reports dwellings.

Unmodelled rules register: rule, zones, reason, likely effect of modelling it (overstates / understates / either), size where known.

3.3 Conditions available to any rule

min/max site area; rear sites only / not; within N m of frontage (tested at segment midpoint, documented) or share of depth; adjacent zone(s) or not; above storey / height; boundary orientation; variant; activity status. Conditions that cannot be evaluated (missing layer) follow the project rule: not applied, counted, and warned with the direction of the error.

3.4 Jurisdiction-neutral details

  • Units: metres internally; units = "ft" accepted on input and output (Q7). Sites must be in a projected CRS; geographic CRS is an error.
  • Hemisphere inferred from the CRS / centroid for orientation rules, overridable.
  • zone_map: the jurisdiction’s own zone codes/labels → rulebook zone keys (the alias map), with a check that every mapped zone is either modelled or listed as unmodelled (no silent zero).

3.5 Combining overlapping rules, and rules from other jurisdictions

Full analysis in RULES-RESEARCH.md. In summary:

  • Coverage, landscaping and impervious limits combine as the most restrictive, not additively (as capacityengine does now). A ground budget adds the paving a development needs (access legs, surface parking, outdoor space per dwelling). It has three modes: most_restrictive (default), with_access and full. Sites with no slack are flagged. A ground_overlap: block declares which ground may count twice.
  • Seven combination operators: cap, envelope, replace, floor, add, multiply, composite. They are evaluated in a fixed order: zone → areas → overlays → bonuses → entitlements. Variants: by default a site takes the maximum over its permitted variants.
  • Setback profile primitive. Every rule about distance from a boundary becomes d(h) from an origin line (boundary, far side of road, road centreline). Values may be restricted formulas, e.g. max(3, 0.4*H) or road_width*0.4.
  • New triggers (stage 2): road width, slope, distance band to a layer, corner or through site, site dimensions.
  • New in v1: GFA definition; unit mix conversion; parking; coverage by height; bonuses reported separately; buffer exclusions such as trees; minimum floor level.
  • v2 (held as rules and flagged in v1): shadow and sunlight; building depth and separation packing; outlook; amalgamation.

4A. Morphology helpers (user request, 20 Nov)

Identifying what each boundary and site is comes before any rule can apply, and every such identification rests on assumptions (how much road contact makes a frontage, what angle splits side from rear). These get their own exported family, find_*(), so they can be run, inspected, plotted and corrected on their own, before any capacity run.

Helper Identifies Default assumptions (all overridable)
find_road_frontages() Boundaries on a road; frontage length per road Road layer if given, else gap or centreline inference; min road contact 0.5 m; probe distance 25 m to clear carriageways
find_side_rear() Side vs rear boundaries Angle to frontage; tolerance 30°; depth-share rule for ambiguous segments
find_corner_sites() Sites on two or more roads at an angle Corner angle tolerance; min frontage on each road
find_through_sites() Sites with frontage on opposite sides Bearing difference ≥ 135°
find_rear_sites() Rear (battle-axe) sites Frontage below a width threshold or reached only by a leg
find_access_legs() Driveways / access legs, and whether they come off net site area Leg opening 7.5 m max; road contact ≥ 0.5 m; exclude_from_net_area = TRUE
find_rights_of_way() Shared accessways from an easement layer Optional layer; width from geometry
find_internal_boundaries() Common walls / internal boundaries (unit titles, cross-leases, amalgamated sites) Shared-edge overlap fraction, never intersects
find_water_boundaries() Coastal, riparian, lakeside boundaries Distance to water layer; bank vs centreline
find_reserve_boundaries() Boundaries onto open space / reserves Zone family membership across the boundary
find_boundary_runs() Near-straight pieces of one boundary treated as one Merge angle 5°
site_metrics() Area, depth, width, frontage width, compactness, largest inscribed rectangle (site shape factor) —

How assumptions are held:

morphology_defaults()                       # package defaults, documented
rb <- set_morphology(rb, corner_angle_deg = 25, access_leg_max_width_m = 6)
sites <- prepare_sites(parcels, zoning, rulebook = rb,
                       morphology = list(min_road_contact_m = 1))  # run override

Precedence: run argument > rulebook morphology: block > package default. The values actually used are stored on the result, so every run says which definitions it applied. Each helper returns the classification and the evidence (contact length, angle, probe hit), so a wrong call can be traced.

Checking tools:

  • plot_morphology(sites, area = bbox) — boundaries coloured by class, rear sites and access legs hatched, corners marked. The way to eyeball a new jurisdiction’s cadastre before trusting a run.
  • check_morphology(sites) — shares of each class against plausible ranges (the project’s 19% corner-site share was a warning sign worth automating); unclassified segments; inward-normal failures.
  • override_boundaries(sites, segment_id, class) — manual correction table, applied reproducibly (kept as data, not edits to geometry).

4. Site preparation

sites <- prepare_sites(parcels, zoning,
  zone_field = "ZONE", roads = road_parcels,      # or streets = centrelines
  water = rivers, group_by = NULL, terrain = NULL, rulebook = rb)

Steps, each also exported on its own:

  1. clean_parcels() — validity, drop slivers (flagged), drop road/rail/water parcels by a user-supplied filter, projected-CRS check.
  2. split_sites_by_zone() — partition-safe (no 50/50 drop).
  3. classify_boundaries() — segments; road / side / rear / internal by adjacency, road contact and frontage; rear sites and access legs; corner sites; inward normals from the geometry, not vertex order.
  4. resolve_adjacency() — zone across each boundary (pass the WHOLE zoning layer, including open space).
  5. attach_overlays() — area/length overlap fractions, never intersects.
  6. attach_terrain() (optional, terra) — per-segment ground datum.

Result is a cap_sites object (sf + segments table) that can be cached and reused across rule scenarios, because it does not depend on rule values (only on the zoning/overlay layers). That split is what made Auckland’s re-runs fast.

Performance rules baked in: no per-site loops with GEOS calls; STRtree joins; clip lookup geometry to the working extent; chunked runs with optional parallelism (mirai or future, Q10). Target: 50k sites in minutes on a laptop; benchmark script in inst/bench/.

5. Engine and results

cap <- estimate_capacity(sites, rb, variant = "standard",
                         conversion = conversion(dwelling_size = 90))

estimate_capacity() = build_envelopes() + estimate_yield(). Envelope method as in capacityengine: loop storeys, vectorise sites, reduce setbacks/planes/upper-level rules to one required setback per segment, three GEOS calls a storey, test each storey at its ceiling, then caps (coverage as share of SITE area, FAR, floorplate), then stack rules.

The result is a cap_result S3 object:

Slot Content
sites sf, one row per input site: zone, area, method, height, storeys, footprint, GFA, residential GFA, business GFA, dwellings, binding constraint, flags
storeys tibble, site × storey: level, height, floor area, binding constraint
segments optional (keep_setbacks = TRUE): segment × storey setback, winning rule, citation
rulebook, conversion, variant what produced it
meta package version, run time, input hashes, warnings tally

Tidy accessors: as_tibble(cap), sf::st_as_sf(cap), cap_storeys(cap), cap_flags(cap). print(cap) gives a short headline with the “plan-enabled, gross, blank-slate” caveat and the conversion assumption.

Binding constraint per storey (height / plane / setback / coverage / FAR / floorplate / density / overlay) is recorded, because it powers the most useful summary and plot (which rule is doing the work).

6. Summaries

Design goal: one verb with a by argument, sensible defaults, tidy output, and a pretty table on demand.

summary(cap)                                   # headline + by zone
summarise_capacity(cap, by = "zone")           # tibble
summarise_capacity(cap, by = c("zone", "height_band"),
                   measures = c("gfa", "dwellings", "sites", "land_area"))
summarise_capacity(cap, by = "area", areas = suburbs, area_id = "name")
summarise_capacity(cap, by = "storeys")
capacity_table(x)                              # gt table, formatted, sourced

by accepts: any site column (zone, method, variant, overlay flags), derived bins (height_band, storeys, site_size_band, fsr_band), spatial units (areas = polygons, assigned by majority with partition safety; or grid = 500 for a hex/square grid), and binding_constraint.

Measures: sites, land area, footprint, GFA (total / residential / business), dwellings, mean & median per site, FAR achieved, share of total, plus “density” measures per hectare of land.

Other summary functions:

  • constraint_breakdown(cap) — floor area lost to each rule, in sequence from a theoretical maximum (zoned land × height) down to enabled. Feeds the waterfall plot.
  • compare_capacity(a, b, by = "zone") — scenario differences, absolute and %, with a reconciliation check (same site set).
  • sensitivity(sites, rb, rule = "MRZ$height", values = c(11, 14, 16)) — sweeps a rule and returns a tidy table.
  • explain_site(cap, site_id) — boundary-by-boundary table: class, length, setback per storey, winning rule and citation; caps; binding constraint.
  • unmodelled_report(rb) — the register as a table, for any report.
  • check_capacity(cap) — reconciliation and diagnostics (sites in = sites out, zero-capacity sites by reason, flags tally, suspicious values).

7. Plots

All ggplot2, all return ggplot objects (so users can add layers), one theme (theme_capacity()) and one palette system, colour-blind safe, light/dark variants. Labels auto-formatted (m², k / M, %). Captions auto-state “Plan-enabled gross capacity; dwellings at X m² per dwelling”.

Function What it shows
plot_capacity(cap, by = "zone", measure = "gfa") Ranked horizontal bars; fill = second variable for stacks; facet =
plot_height_profile(cap, by = "zone") Floorspace by storey / height band: a “skyline” histogram of where capacity sits vertically
plot_distribution(cap, measure = "dwellings") Per-site distribution (ridgeline / histogram) by zone
plot_constraints(cap) Waterfall from theoretical max to enabled, by rule; or share of storeys bound by each rule, by zone
plot_capacity_map(cap, measure, grid = 250) Choropleth on sites, hex grid or user areas; basemap optional (maptiles)
plot_comparison(a, b, by = "zone") Dumbbell / diverging bars between scenarios
plot_sensitivity(sens) Line/step chart of a rule sweep
plot_cumulative(cap) Capacity curve: cumulative dwellings vs share of land, sites ranked
plot_site(cap, site_id, view = "plan" / "axo") Single site: parcel, setback strips, storey footprints in plan; axonometric stack (ggplot polygons, no 3D dependency)
autoplot(cap) Sensible default dashboard (patchwork of 4)

Optional interactive layer (Suggests only): view_capacity_3d(cap) with mapgl (MapLibre extrusions) — the visual language already proven in the capacity viewer. Q11 decides whether this is v1 or later.

The plotting look gets its own design pass at stage 6 with rendered examples reviewed before release (house rule: verify against the rendered output, not the code).

8. Example data and documentation

Example data (Q5). A synthetic town, “Exampleton”: ~2,000 parcels with roads, five zones, a height overlay, a precinct, a river, an exclusion, plus its rulebook in YAML and XLSX. Synthetic means no licence questions and it can be built to exercise every rule (corner sites, rear lots, adjacency, bands). Optionally a small real NZ extract (LINZ data is CC BY 4.0) as a second, realistic dataset.

Documentation (CRAN standard):

  • roxygen2 on every exported function, with runnable examples on Exampleton (fast, < 5 s each).
  • Vignettes:
    1. Getting started — parcels to plots in ten lines.
    2. Writing a rulebook — the three entry routes, validation, citations.
    3. Rule reference — every rule type, a diagram each, how it is computed.
    4. Preparing sites — boundary classes, adjacency, terrain, pitfalls.
    5. Summaries and plots — gallery.
    6. Scenarios, sensitivity and comparison.
    7. Adding a new jurisdiction — worked example from plan text to results.
    8. Method and assumptions — what “plan-enabled” means, what it is not, the unmodelled register, validation against published studies.
  • pkgdown site (GitHub Pages), README with badges, NEWS.md, CITATION, CONTRIBUTING, Code of Conduct, issue templates (incl. “new jurisdiction”).
  • inst/rulebooks/ holds contributed rulebooks; the Auckland, Christchurch and Wellington bundles converted as worked, real examples (Q6).

Quality: testthat 3e (port the ~1,000 expectations that apply), covr target > 85%, R CMD check clean (0/0/0) on GitHub Actions for Windows, macOS, Linux × release/devel/oldrel, lintr, urlchecker, spelling. Benchmarks guard against quadratic regressions.

9. Dependencies

Imports (lean): sf, geos, wk, dplyr, tibble, vctrs, rlang, cli, yaml, jsonlite, jsonvalidate, ggplot2, scales. Suggests: terra (terrain, surfaces), readxl/openxlsx2 (XLSX rulebooks), gt (tables), patchwork (autoplot), ggridges, maptiles/tidyterra (basemaps), mapgl (3D), mirai (parallel), arrow/sfarrow (caching), testthat, knitr, rmarkdown/quarto. Everything optional is checked with rlang::check_installed().

10. Stages and gates

Stage Deliverable Gate
0 Name, repo, skeleton (usethis), CI, licence, Exampleton data CI green on 3 OSes
1 Rulebook: schema, R constructors, YAML/JSON I/O, validation, print/rule_table Auckland/CHC/WCC bundles convert and validate; round-trip tests
2 Site preparation Ported boundary/adjacency tests pass; Exampleton prepared
3 Envelope engine Hand-checked cases reproduce exactly (S039789 etc.); benchmark
4 Yield paths, overlays, areas, variants, conversion A capacityengine region tile reproduces to the m²
5 Summaries, compare, sensitivity, explain_site Reconciliation checks; vignettes 1, 5, 6 draft
6 Plots + theme design pass Rendered gallery reviewed by you
7 XLSX template entry, new-jurisdiction vignette, docs, pkgdown A fresh jurisdiction entered from the template end to end
8 Release: public repo, pkgdown live, (CRAN submission if Q8) R CMD check 0/0/0; you sign off

The reproducibility gate at stage 4 is the main safeguard: the new package must match capacityengine on the same inputs before it is trusted.

11. Decisions (20 November 2026)

# Question Decision
Q1 Name plancap
Q2 Relation to capacityengine Clean new package; port algorithms and tests; capacityengine untouched, may depend on plancap later
Q2a Morphology Dedicated find_*() helpers with defaults, overridable (section 4A)
Q3 Rule entry All three: YAML/JSON, R constructors, XLSX template
Q4 Licence MIT
Q5 Example data Synthetic “Exampleton” + small real NZ extract (LINZ CC BY 4.0)
Q6 NZ rulebooks Ship Auckland, Christchurch, Wellington as dated worked examples in inst/rulebooks/
Q7 Units Metres internally; feet / sq ft accepted on input and output
Q8 CRAN CRAN-standard (0/0/0, full docs) on GitHub first; submission decided after v1
Q9 GitHub owner faceteconomics (you may need to create the empty repo; I push)
Q10 Parallel In v1, mirai chunked runs
Q11 Interactive 3D In v1, mapgl (Suggests)
Q12 Net of existing In v1, when existing floorspace / dwellings are supplied
Q13 Terrain In v1, terra (Suggests)
Q14 Plot style Neutral, themeable default; optional theme_facet()
Q15 Morphology defaults Held in the rulebook, overridable per run
Q19 Coverage vs landscaping Most restrictive, not additive; ground budget default mode most_restrictive (paving = 0, matches capacityengine); with_access and full opt-in; no-slack sites flagged
Q20 Variants Site result = max over permitted variants; every variant kept
Q21 Bonuses Reported in separate *_with_bonus columns; base figure has no bonus
Q22 Shadow / sunlight v2; v1 holds the rule and flags affected sites

Consequences for the stages: terrain and morphology move into stage 2; net-of-existing into stage 4; parallel runs into stage 3; mapgl view into stage 6; the XLSX template into stage 1 (it shares the schema).
